title: The work-type enum and the factory's work-type to model table
description:
The vocabulary and the price list, which are deliberately two things.

The enum is settled and is in this epic's parent description: mechanical, translation, construction, diagnosis, design - ordered on the axis of how much must be worked out rather than carried out. Declare it as a closed enum the way the tier vocabulary already is (isKnownTier refuses anything else); a work type that is not one of these is a bug, not a fallback.

The table maps work type -> model and lives in FACTORY CONFIG beside the existing [roles.*.tiers.*] overlays, because a work type is another key into that kind of table. With today's two models the mapping is mechanical/translation/construction -> glm-5.3-flash and diagnosis/design -> glm-5.3.

Two rules the table must obey:
  - A work type with no mapping falls back to the default AND SAYS SO. Failing a dispatch on a table someone forgot to extend is the wrong failure.
  - Changing the table must not invalidate a recorded classification. That separation is the whole reason Jev is asked what the work IS rather than what it is worth - so nothing may write a model name where a work type belongs.

No model call in this tick. This is vocabulary and config only.
acceptance_criteria: A closed work-type enum refuses an unknown value, factory config maps each work type to a model, an unmapped work type resolves to the default and is reported as having done so, and go test -short ./... passes
